To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) contrastive learning is an effective approach for unsupervised video representation learning; (b) spatial and temporal augmentations are both crucial to the performance of contrastive learning; and (c) the temporal consistency of spatial augmentations is important for contrastive video representation learning.

(1) self supervised video representation learning is possible, and can achieve performance close to supervised pre training; (2) spatial and temporal augmentations are both important; (3) temporal augmentations can be implemented by applying the same spatial augmentation to all frames in a video; and (4) the performance gap between self supervised and supervised pre training can be closed by using a larger backbone.
